title: Developing Taste in Coding Agents: Applied Meta Neuro-Symbolic RL — Ahmad Awais, CommandCode
talk_summary: Command Code demos a coding agent that learns a developer's 'taste' from edits and feedback, stores it in a transparent taste file/meta neuro-symbolic layer, and injects it into future runs to reduce steering. The talk is mostly product demo and claims, with little implementation detail or rigorous evaluation.

takeaways.what_they_do: It watches how the developer edits AI-generated code and records recurring preferences such as libraries, file layout, and versioning in a transparent taste file, then feeds those preferences into later coding runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it has seen me go and edit AI code and fix it this way

takeaways.what_they_do: It continuously updates learned rules when the developer's preferences change, rather than requiring manual edits to static rules files.
takeaways.evidence_quote: now Emmeth prefers to use commander over meow

takeaways.what_they_do: It uses the same learned taste to generate and review code, aiming to catch non-correctness preferences and reduce review time.
takeaways.numbers: 10x merged code; review time down significantly

takeaways.technique: Encode repeated taste as deterministic checks
takeaways.what_they_do: It claims to combine the probabilistic LLM with a deterministic neuro-symbolic layer that enforces learned preferences and guardrails.
takeaways.evidence_quote: neuros symbolic space to enforce that invisible logic

takeaways.what_they_do: It packages learned taste as installable/shareable packs so a team or borrowed expert preferences can be applied to coding agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: npx taste and install my CLI taste
